series.label: The series
series.headline: Five straight for Georgia
series.line: FloridaGators.com counts the series at Georgia 57, Florida 44, two ties, starting in 1915. The Bulldogs have won the last five, all in Jacksonville, by a combined 177-87: 34-7 in 2021, 42-20 in 2022, 43-20 in 2023, 34-20 in 2024 and 24-20 last Nov. 1. Florida's last win was 44-28 in 2020; the Gators are 2-8 in the last 10.
series.source: FloridaGators.com, football opponent history vs. Georgia (44-57-2, streak L5, last 10: 2-8; the 2025 final confirmed on ESPN, event 401752755). Georgia's own count includes a disputed 1904 game and reads 58-44-2.

keys.label: Four keys

items.h: Baugh against the best run defense he has seen
items.p: Jadan Baugh has 763 yards and 13 touchdowns on 135 carries, and Florida runs for 194.3 a game. Georgia allows 90.3 rushing yards a game at 2.8 a carry, both the lowest figures on this page.
Georgia converts 54.0% of its third downs and holds opponents to 35.9%. Florida converts 44.6% and allows 43.7%. The Gators' defense has 22 sacks to Georgia's 22, and Georgia has allowed only 8.

items.h: Stockton against a pass defense that allows 255 a game
items.p: Gunner Stockton is 117 of 158 for 1,570 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions; Georgia completes 71.6% at 9.7 yards an attempt. Florida allows 255.0 passing yards a game.

items.h: The quarterback Sumrall will not name
items.p: Aaron Philo is 105 of 149 for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions this season; Tramell Jones Jr. made his first start in the 27-24 win at Texas. Sumrall said Monday he is not telling Georgia who starts. Dallas Wilson leads the receivers with 29 catches for 403 yards.

lead.label: The Lead
lead.author: Franz Beard
lead.title: Thoughts of the Day: Sumrall's first Florida-Georgia
lead.html:
"I think anybody that says it's just another game doesn't have a real good pulse of what reality is in college football or to our fan base."

Jon Sumrall said that Monday at his press conference at the Heavener Football Center in Gainesville, a combination of excitement and reverence showing on his face and in his demeanor. Saturday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta (3:30 p.m., ABC) will be his first Florida-Georgia game. The fact that the game will be played somewhere other than Jacksonville, the long-standing traditional home of the rivalry game does nothing to dampen his enthusiasm or his understanding of what winning this game means.

It is more, much more, than border state bragging rights and the importance goes far beyond two ranked teams squaring off, both of them very much in the hunt for a second trip to Atlanta this season for the SEC Championship Game and beyond that, the College Football Playoff. For the 17th-ranked Gators (5-2, 3-2 SEC), a loss would jeopardize their chances of making the SEC Championship Game for the first time since 2020 and reaching the College Football Playoff for the first time. The four-team playoff introduced in 2014 expanded to 12 teams in 2024. For No. 3 Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC), it is a matter of keeping up with the SEC Joneses, in this case the rather surprising Kentucky Wildcats (7-1, 5-1 SEC). Since 2011 Georgia has played for the SEC championship 10 times, winning four, all of them since Kirby Smart became the head coach. The Bulldogs broke a 41-year national championship drought in 2021 and repeated in 2022.

Georgia has it. It is Sumrall's job to restore some sanity (that's from the Florida perspective) to the rivalry. More than half the players who will suit up for Florida Saturday have never played in this game. They came to Florida from the transfer portal or as wide-eyed freshmen. Georgia's program under Smart has grown to a point of using the portal only to add a few impact players each year. Nearly the entire roster is home grown.

To put that in perspective, Georgia has won five consecutive games against Florida. The Gators last beat the Bulldogs in 2020.

feature.label: The Big Picture
feature.kicker: Brenden Martin on GameDay and Kirby
feature.author: Brenden Martin
feature.title: Snubbed in Atlanta: GameDay passed, Kirby shrugged, Florida noticed
feature.dek: College GameDay went to Bloomington, Kirby Smart called Florida's quarterbacks "completely capable," and the rivalry moved 70 miles from his campus. Brenden Martin reads the transcripts.

image.alt: Florida and Georgia players converge on a ball carrier during the Nov. 2, 2024, rivalry game in Jacksonville. File photo by Chris Spears, GatorBait Media.
image.credit: Photo by Chris Spears, GatorBait Media

feature.caption: Florida and Georgia in Jacksonville, Nov. 2, 2024. File photo.
feature.html:
I am not a detective. I read college football press conference transcripts for a living, which is a worse job and, this week, nearly the same one.

Because something about this Florida-Georgia week does not add up, and it is not the point spread.

Begin with the smallest mystery. ESPN's College GameDay is a show that travels the country looking for the biggest game in America, and this week it found one in Bloomington, Indiana, where the Hoosiers will host Minnesota. Minnesota is 5-2. The Gophers are a perfectly respectable football team, the kind you are happy to see on your schedule in November, preferably at noon, preferably already over. Indiana is the defending national champion and ranked No. 4, so the show is not crazy. It is just not at our game, and our game is Florida and Georgia, in Atlanta, for the first time in the modern history of the rivalry.

Georgia, for the record, has already been on the show this year. GameDay went to Tuscaloosa for Georgia and Alabama in Week 6. The Bulldogs have had their close-up. It was the rivalry itself, a hundred years old and temporarily homeless, that got left at the curb in a nice suit. The SEC's own pregame show will be in Atlanta on Saturday morning, Tim Tebow and all. The big one will be at a fountain in Bloomington.

Which brings us to the main witness. Kirby Smart met the media on Monday, and I have now read his remarks three times. This tells you nothing good about my social life and a great deal about his adjectives.

Kirby was warm about nearly everyone. Jon Sumrall has brought energy and physicality to Florida. The coordinators have his respect. Buster Faulkner, once an assistant on Kirby's own staff, was introduced like family at a reunion: one of the best offensive minds in the country, a close friend, respect upon respect. If compliments were currency, Buster could retire.

Then Kirby arrived at Florida's quarterbacks. He called Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. "very talented" and "good players," credited their wins and said Faulkner can play to their strengths. Fair enough. But a man has to know what he heard, and what I heard was "completely capable," followed by "plenty capable." The way you describe a rental car. It has four wheels. It runs. It is completely capable of reaching the airport.

Oh, and just one more thing. In Buster's offense, Kirby explained, "it doesn't require the quarterback to be perfect."

There it is. Everything else in that press conference was a man being gracious. To my ear, that sentence sounded more revealing than the compliments. He respects the machine. The two young men operating it, the ones who beat Ole Miss and Texas, are simply the help. Kirby even recited their accomplishments himself, both wins, out loud, and then handed them the same word you would use for a hotel shower with decent water pressure.
